faq.q: Why does the room keep spinning when I stop?
faq.a: The fluid in your inner ear keeps moving for a few seconds after you stop, so your balance organs still report turning. Your brain believes them and the room appears to spin.
asks: Why do I feel like I am still spinning?
Why does dizziness last after spinning?

faq.q: Why does the dizzy feeling fade if I keep spinning?
faq.a: Once you spin at a steady speed, the fluid in the canals catches up and moves with you. With no fluid lagging behind, the hair cells stop signalling and the sense of turning fades.
asks: Why don't I feel the spin after a while?
Do you get used to spinning?

faq.q: How do ballet dancers avoid getting dizzy?
faq.a: Dancers use spotting: they fix their eyes on one point and whip the head round quickly at the last moment. This keeps the eyes steady most of the time, and training also teaches the brain to pay less attention to the false signals.
asks: How do skaters spin without getting dizzy?

faq.q: Why does dizziness make people feel sick?
faq.a: When your eyes and inner ears disagree about movement, the brain gets confusing signals. One idea is that the brain treats this mismatch as a warning sign and triggers nausea. The same mismatch causes travel sickness.
asks: Why does spinning make me feel sick?

faq.q: Why do my eyes flick after spinning?
faq.a: Your balance system tries to keep your eyes steady by moving them against the spin it thinks is happening. The eyes drift and then flick back, over and over, which is called nystagmus.
asks: Why do eyes jiggle when you are dizzy?

facts: The jerky eye movements seen after spinning are called nystagmus.
Dancers and figure skaters use a technique called spotting to reduce dizziness during turns.
